Synthetic lycopene dispersed in oil showed only ~1.2% of the dose appearing in blood circulation in humans.
Phytoene was estimated to be 58% bioavailable in humans, providing a high-bioavailability example among long-chain isoprenoids, but it lacks the polar quinone head of the query.
A 13C-lycopene study reported 23.2% bioavailability for all-trans lycopene, an above-threshold estimate, but this is an outlier relative to most lycopene systemic-availability measurements.

High-bioavailability examples such as phytoene are less transferable because they lack the polar quinone head. Therefore F is more likely below 20%.
evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement is available for the exact ubiquinone-like query molecule.
Formulation effects are not captured; ubiquinone bioavailability can be formulation-dependent.
Human data for tocotrienol and lycopene are indirect and do not exactly match the quinone head group of the query.
